summary: Temporary support role provisioning blocked when Okta secondaryEmail marked 'hidden' — SCIM PATCH rejected
description: Issue summary: Users requesting Temporary Support Role via internal approval flow fail to receive the role when their Okta profile has a secondaryEmail element that is set to 'hidden'. The SCIM PATCH generated by our identity-provisioner is rejected by the internal RBAC API with a 422/validation error citing unexpected attribute format. Impact: multiple engineers could not elevate to the emergency support role during a Friday afternoon oncall rotation; manual provisioning was required.
impact: On-call engineers unable to get short-lived support role via self-serve approval; delays ~15-45 minutes per user due to manual provisioning. Affected team: Support & SRE rotations. No customer-facing outage but elevated operational risk.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Ensure Okta user profile has secondaryEmail element present and marked with 'visibility': 'hidden' in the profile (this can happen via certain IdP imports).
2) As a user, trigger Temporary Support Role request from /internal/approvals -> request 'support:temporary-admin' and complete manager approval flow.
3) Observe the identity-provisioner logs: it sends a SCIM PATCH to /internal-identity/provision with payload that includes secondaryEmail in the patch body.
4) RBAC API responds with 422 ValidationError: 'attribute secondaryEmail: unrecognized format' and the provisioning job fails; the user does not receive role membership.
5) Manual workaround: SRE manually adds role via admin console; job then retries but subsequent automatic retries still fail.
Expected: Temporary role should be created without the SCIM PATCH failing for hidden secondaryEmail.
logs: 2026-03-12T15:23:41Z identity-provisioner INFO sending PATCH /v2/users/7234 - payload keys: [name, emails, groups, meta]
2026-03-12T15:23:41Z rbac-api ERROR 422 ValidationError: 'emails.secondary.visibility' unexpected value 'hidden' for attribute 'secondaryEmail' (requestId=5f8c-9b2d)
2026-03-12T15:40:02Z support-bot INFO manual role add: admin added support:temporary-admin to user a.patel@example.com (performed by samira.chen)
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: SCIM consumer (rbac-api) expects a different structure for secondary / hidden emails; our provisioner forwards Okta's attribute verbatim.
Checked Okta SCIM mapping: secondaryEmail lands in 'emails' array with an extra 'visibility' key when Okta profile field configured as 'internal' or migrated from legacy IdP.
Reproduced locally by creating a test Okta user with secondaryEmail visibility:hidden and submitting approval flow — got same 422 from rbac-api.
Reviewed rbac-api schema: it accepts emails[] with attributes value,type,primary; unknown keys cause strict schema rejection. Previously unseen 'visibility' field triggers schema validation failure.
Workaround validated: modify provisioner to strip unknown keys from emails[] before PATCH — immediate success for role creation in test env.

Root cause: Okta idP import introduced a non-standard metadata key 'visibility' on secondaryEmail which our strict RBAC API rejects. The identity-provisioner forwards full Okta payload without sanitization.
Probability of recurrence: high for users migrated from legacy IdP or for Okta workflows that set field visibility flags.

2) If frequent, use CLI admin tool: `adminctl add-role --user a.patel@example.com --role support:temporary-admin` and confirm in /internal/roles.
3) Avoid mass automated retries; disable provisioning job for the single user and rely on manual until canary sanitizer deploy completes.
